newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: First Tsumeb copper expected by mid-Dec.
newsitem.headline: First Tsumeb copper expected by mid-Dec.

text.p: Tsumeb Corp Ltd (TCL) expects to produce its first copper by mid-December after a crippling strike shut down operations more than two months ago, mine manager Tony de Beer said on Wednesday.
De Beer said TCL completed the retrenchment of about 470 workers on Tuesday and expected production at the company's three mines -- Kombat, Otjihase and Khusib -- to start on December 2.
"All the mines will start production on December 2," he told Reuters by telephone from Namibia.
De Beer said repair work to the copper smelter -- badly damaged during the six-week strike which began on August 23 -- would be completed around the same time.
But the smelter would only start producing copper in the middle of December because of an extended heating up process.
"We should start producing copper around December 12 to December 15," de Beer said.

Owners Gold Fields Namibia Ltd said last Friday that the strike contributed to poor third quarter results. Gold Fields reported a 25.17 million Namibian dollar loss for the quarter ending September 30.
De Beer said the final commissioning of the new Ausmelt lead smelter would take place around January 27.
He said TCL's production loss remained at about 80 tonnes of copper and 80 tonnes of lead.
The strike, which saw workers damage the copper smelter and take control of parts of the mine, had been a learning experience for management and the workers, de Beer said.
"It will be at least five or six years before anybody thinks about it (strike action) again," he said.
De Beer added that Namibian President Sam Nujoma said during a visit to the mine on Tuesday that the strike had harmed Namibia's economy,
"He (Nujoma) said the whole country's economy felt the effect of the strike."
De Beer said TCL planned to produce around 2,300 tonnes of copper a month next year and that output over the year would be around 27,000-28,000 tonnes.
The mine expected to produce around 30,000 tonnes of lead in 1997.
TCL produced just under 30,000 tonnes of blister copper last year and 27,000 tonnes of lead. Most of the lead was produced from bought-in material while copper output was from the three mines.
